newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Street murders mar Christmas Eve in Saigon.
newsitem.headline: Street murders mar Christmas Eve in Saigon.

text.p: Two people died and one was seriously wounded in scuffles on the streets of Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City on Christmas Eve, the Thanh Nien newspaper said on Saturday.

Police in the southern city declined to comment on the report, which said one man was stabbed repeatedly with broken bottles and knives by 10 youths after he tried to stop them stealing cigarettes from a store.
Another died after a brawl between eight youths, one of whom was stabbed in the throat and was taken to hospital for emergency treatment.
Ho Chi Minh City, home to many of the country's approximately seven million Roman Catholics, is always a scene of youthful exuberance and celebration on Christmas Eve.
In the capital Hanoi, police arrested 37 people on Christmas Eve as thousands roared around the edge of the picturesque Hoan Kiem Lake on motorbikes.
The official Hanoi Moi daily said police suspected an illegal motorbike race was being organised.

Motorbike racing has become popular among Vietnam's increasingly prosperous urban youth. Nine bikers died this month in the southern resort town of Vung Tau when they slammed into the side of a container during a nightime race.
